paper_metadata.title: Influence of the Co/Ni Ratio and Dendritic Segregations on the High-Temperature Oxidation Resistance of Multinary Co-Rich Superalloys at 850 °C and 1050 °C

evidence.quote: we compare the high-temperature oxidation behavior of two complex Co-rich multinary single-crystalline γ/γ′-strengthened superalloys that only differ regarding their Co/Ni ratios to the commercial Ni-base superalloy CMSX-4

attributes.location: internal oxidation zone and scale/alloy interface

evidence.quote: Within the IOZ, dark oxide particles are embedded that are exemplarily labeled in Figures 5(b) and (d). Since the BSE contrast is linked to the average atomic mass of a phase, and since alumina is the lightest oxide for both alloys that is expected to grow, these spots can consequently be identified as alumina
The micrographs demonstrate three laterally aligned Cr-enriched regions (Figure 12). Whereas the upper two are strongly pronounced and resemble actual layers,
Obviously, the outer oxide layer that developed on dendritic regions of ERBOCo-1 (Figure 12) is composed of Co, Ni, and oxygen.

Similar to the oxidation at 850 °C, nitrides can be found below the IOF. The latter are clearly enriched in Hf and Ti but not in Al what matches well with the results from other groups that stated a higher thermodynamic stability of HfN and TiN as compared to AlN.

attributes.composition: Co, Cr, W enriched in dendrite cores; Ni, Al, Ti, Ta, Si, Hf enriched in interdendritic regions

evidence.quote: In AC state for the interdendritic regions, above-average contents of Ni, Al, Ti, Ta, Si, and Hf are clearly seen, whereas Co, Cr, and W are strongly enriched in the dendrite cores

Below the outer oxide layer an IOZ of distinct alumina precipitates prevails at least locally. The latter is not effective in retarding the inward penetration of reactive species (oxygen or nitrogen).
Below the IOZ, a γ′-depleted zone is allocated which is exemplarily marked in Figure 5(a) by means of a white line.
The SEM-based analysis indicates the development of rather inhomogeneous oxide scales.

attributes.location: below external oxide scale, especially in dendritic regions

evidence.quote: The dendrite cores demonstrate an apparently porous IOZ at the fracture surface.
Furthermore, it is noteworthy that prolonging the exposure duration from 100 to 500 hours effectuated the growth of large pores within the substrate.
After 500 hours of oxidation, however, the stress level inside the oxide scale during cooling surpassed a critical level that led to complete separation of the upper scale section from the substrate.

It is assumed that especially the refractory metals (W and Ta) might be causative as the latter strongly segregate during solidification and as they are known to affect the oxidation resistance.
